[Pairs · 8 minutes · your homework]{.act-label}

::: {.prompt}
Tell your neighbor the two plant variables you chose. Do they rise and fall together? Is one driving the other, or does something else move both?
:::

::: {.checks3}
::: {.c4}
[1 · The pair]{.label}

:::
::: {.c4}

:::

  const W = 1160, H = 380, L = 78, R = 20, T = 16, B = 52, n = D.temp.length;
  const grid = (ys, V, fmt) => ys.map((v) => `<line x1="${L}" x2="${W - R}" y1="${V(v)}" y2="${V(v)}" stroke="#B9C1C6"/><text x="${L - 10}" y="${V(v) + 6}" text-anchor="end" font-size="17" fill="#333F4A">${fmt(v)}</text>`).join('');
  const frame = (xl, yl) => `<line x1="${L}" x2="${L}" y1="${T}" y2="${H - B}" stroke="#333F4A" stroke-width="1.5"/><line x1="${L}" x2="${W - R}" y1="${H - B}" y2="${H - B}" stroke="#333F4A" stroke-width="1.5"/><text x="${(L + W - R) / 2}" y="${H - 8}" text-anchor="middle" font-size="16" fill="#66727C">${xl}</text><text transform="translate(20 ${(T + H - B) / 2}) rotate(-90)" text-anchor="middle" font-size="16" fill="#66727C">${yl}</text>`;
  const ramp = (k) => { const t = k / (n - 1); const a = [185, 222, 219], b = [8, 62, 60]; return `rgb(${a.map((c, i) => Math.round(c + (b[i] - c) * t)).join(',')})`; };
  function scatter(xs, ys, xr, yr, xt, yt, xl, yl, r) {
    const X = (v) => L + ((v - xr[0]) / (xr[1] - xr[0])) * (W - L - R), V = (v) => T + (1 - (v - yr[0]) / (yr[1] - yr[0])) * (H - T - B);
    const mn = (v) => String(v).replace('-', '−');
    let g = grid(yt, V, mn) + xt.map((v) => `<text x="${X(v)}" y="${H - B + 22}" text-anchor="middle" font-size="17" fill="#333F4A">${mn(v)}</text>`).join('') + frame(xl, yl);
    xs.forEach((x, k) => { const y = ys[k]; if (x === null || y === null) return; g += `<circle cx="${X(x).toFixed(1)}" cy="${V(y).toFixed(1)}" r="7" fill="${ramp(k)}" stroke="#fff" stroke-width="1"/>`; });
    g += `<text x="${W - R - 8}" y="${T + 24}" text-anchor="end" font-size="24" font-weight="700" fill="#1C242B">r = ${r}</text>`;
    return g;
  }
  function series() {
    const z = (xs) => { const v = xs.filter((x) => x !== null), m = v.reduce((s, x) => s + x, 0) / v.length, sd = Math.sqrt(v.reduce((s, x) => s + (x - m) ** 2, 0) / (v.length - 1)); return (x) => (x - m) / sd; };
    const zt = z(D.temp), zn = z(D.nox);
    const X = (k) => L + (k / (n - 1)) * (W - L - R), V = (v) => T + (1 - (v + 3) / 6) * (H - T - B);
    let g = grid([-2, 0, 2], V, (v) => (v > 0 ? '+' + v : String(v).replace('-', '−'))) + frame('2004', 'standard deviations from mean');
    [['2004-07-01', 11], ['2004-08-01', 42], ['2004-09-01', 73], ['2004-10-01', 103]].forEach(([d, k]) => { g += `<text x="${X(k)}" y="${H - B + 22}" text-anchor="middle" font-size="17" fill="#333F4A">1/${d.slice(5, 7)}</text>`; });
    const path = (xs, f, attr) => { let d = '', pen = false; xs.forEach((v, k) => { if (v === null) { pen = false; return; } d += (pen ? 'L' : 'M') + X(k).toFixed(1) + ',' + V(f(v)).toFixed(1); pen = true; }); return `<path d="${d}" fill="none" ${attr}/>`; };
    g += path(D.temp, zt, 'stroke="#0F6E6B" stroke-width="2"') + path(D.nox, zn, 'stroke="#E29A2D" stroke-width="2.5"');
    g += path(D.tT, zt, 'stroke="#0A4E4C" stroke-width="3" stroke-dasharray="8 6"') + path(D.tN, zn, 'stroke="#9a5f10" stroke-width="3" stroke-dasharray="8 6"');
    g += `<text x="${L + 12}" y="${T + 22}" font-size="18" fill="#0F6E6B" font-weight="600">temperature</text><text x="${L + 140}" y="${T + 22}" font-size="18" fill="#9a5f10" font-weight="600">NOx</text><text x="${L + 200}" y="${T + 22}" font-size="17" fill="#66727C">dashed: 29-day trend</text>`;
    return g;
  }
  const NOTE = {
    raw: '77 days with both. r = −0.57: cooler days had more NOx. Darker points are later in the window.',
    time: 'Temperature stays near 29 °C until mid-September, then falls. NOx is lowest in August and rises sharply in September. Both follow the calendar.',
    det: 'Each value minus its own 29-day trend (70 days). r = 0.14: the day-to-day changes hardly move together.',
  };
  function draw(v) {
    let g;
    if (v === 'raw') g = scatter(D.temp, D.nox, [16, 34], [0, 400], [20, 25, 30], [0, 100, 200, 300, 400], 'daily mean temperature, °C', 'daily mean NOx, ppb', '−0.57');
    else if (v === 'det') g = scatter(D.dT, D.dN, [-8, 6], [-200, 150], [-6, -4, -2, 0, 2, 4], [-200, -100, 0, 100], 'temperature minus its trend, °C', 'NOx minus its trend, ppb', '0.14');
    else g = series();
    document.getElementById('rl-plot').innerHTML = g;
    document.getElementById('rl-out').textContent = NOTE[v];
    root.querySelectorAll('[data-v]').forEach((b) => b.setAttribute('aria-pressed', b.dataset.v === v));
  }
  root.querySelectorAll('[data-v]').forEach((b) => b.addEventListener('click', () => draw(b.dataset.v)));
  draw('raw');
})();
</script>

## What r measures {#r-means}

::: {.checks3}
::: {.c4}
[What it is]{.label}
How closely the points follow one straight line, from −1 to +1. The sign gives the direction.
:::
::: {.c4}
[What it is not]{.label}
Not the slope, not the size of an effect, and not a direction of cause. r = −0.57 does not say temperature changes NOx.
:::
::: {.c4}
[What feeds it]{.label}
Any variation the two series share. A slow trend that both follow, over weeks, can produce most of r.
:::
:::

[r² = 0.32 is often read as "temperature explains 32 % of NOx". That sentence claims a cause the number cannot carry.]{.note-line}

For each pair: does one drive the other, does something else move both, or can you not tell? Say what you would check.
:::

## Checks before a cause {#checks}

::: {.checks4}
::: {.c4}
[Remove what both share]{.label}
Subtract each series' slow trend, or compare like with like: same hour, same load, same season.
:::
::: {.c4}
[Look at the timing]{.label}
A cause comes first. Does one series change before the other, by a consistent lag?
:::
::: {.c4}
[Name a mechanism]{.label}
Write the physical or chemical reason. If you cannot, say "associated with", not "causes".
:::
::: {.c4}
[Change it on purpose]{.label}
A planned step test or trial settles what observation cannot. Weeks 6 and 7.
:::
:::

[A small r after removing the trend does not prove "no effect" either. It says the day-to-day data show little. Lab 05, Step 8 asks you to explain this.]{.note-line}
